title: FSS protected ONVIF site bindings v1
description: Strict operator input binding a canonical site manifest to historical private ONVIF handoffs, expected onboarding/profile digests and independently declared RTSP scope. The complete UTF-8 document is bounded to 1 MiB. Each ONVIF source appears exactly once, with no foreign or duplicate sources. A handoff is historical operator configuration, not proof that the manifest HTTP service produced it, current liveness, rights or capture authority. Native code checks all cross-field relations before releasing a complete plan.

manifest_digest.description: Exact canonical digest of the original site manifest, including its independent ONVIF HTTP endpoints and source generations.

sources.description: Native validation requires complete unique coverage of manifest ONVIF sources. Empty is valid only when there are no ONVIF sources. Binding order does not change manifest order.

source_file.description: Absolute private handoff path with a filename and no control, dot or parent components. The Linux owner also checks exact canonical path, regular-file identity, owner-read permission, no group/other permissions, one hard link and unchanged identity. Only complete stable Media1 AVC or indefinite Media2 AVC/HEVC handoffs up to 8192 bytes are retained; aggregate handoff bytes are at most 524288. No file is opened by schema validation.

source_digest.description: SHA-256 of the complete protected handoff bytes, including their original encoding. Native approval separately binds the actual file fingerprint.

onboarding_plan.description: Independent expected historical onboarding-plan digest, compared exactly with the handoff. This comparison does not authenticate an HTTP origin.

profile_digest.description: Independent expected SHA-256 of the exact selected ONVIF profile token, compared with the handoff and bound into stream/operation identities. Stable sensor identity remains the original site/source coordinate.

rtsp_peer.description: Explicit literal IPv4:port or [IPv6]:port RTSP endpoint. Native parsing requires a literal SocketAddr, a valid nonzero port and an admitted peer; it does not resolve DNS or derive this endpoint from the ONVIF HTTP address.

rtsp_authority.description: Exact independently supplied RTSP authority, compared byte-for-byte with the protected handoff. Native validation binds any literal IP and explicit/default RTSP port to rtsp_peer.

control_root.description: Explicit query-free capture control subtree, validated by the existing site/native URI rules and required to contain the exact selected presentation path. This field can itself contain a private capability; protect the binding document. Generated argv contains only its SHA-256, resolved to one exact ancestor of the protected handoff path without normalization or fallback.
